label: Election of Clement VII
why: The campaign start: the cardinals at Fondi elect Clement VII against Urban VI and the Western Schism begins.

realms.name: Kingdom of England
realms.ruler: Richard II (aged 11; government by council, John of Gaunt dominant)
realms.note: Holds Calais, Gascony (Bordeaux–Bayonne), Brest; the Lordship of Ireland. At war with France and Castile.

realms.name: Kingdom of France
realms.ruler: Charles V the Wise (constable Bertrand du Guesclin)
realms.note: Reconquest of English Aquitaine largely done (1369–75); Navarrese lands in Normandy being seized in 1378.

realms.name: Duchy of Brittany
realms.ruler: John IV de Montfort (in exile in England since 1373)
realms.note: Most of the duchy under French royal occupation; Charles V's court confiscates it in Dec 1378; Brest held by England.

realms.name: Duchy of Burgundy
realms.note: Apanage of the Valois; heir by marriage to Flanders, Artois and the county of Burgundy (inherits 1384).

realms.name: County of Flanders
realms.note: Also holds Artois, Nevers, Rethel and the Franche-Comté; Ghent revolt begins 1379.

realms.name: Kingdom of Navarre
realms.note: His Norman counties (Évreux, Cotentin) seized by Charles V in spring 1378; Cherbourg leased to England.

realms.name: Crown of Castile
realms.note: French ally; Castilian galleys raid the English coast. Henry dies 29 May 1379.

realms.name: Crown of Aragon
realms.note: Aragon, Catalonia, Valencia, Majorca; war with Arborea in Sardinia; claims Sicily and Athens.

realms.name: Marinid Sultanate
realms.ruler: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad (Marinid sultan at Fez, raised with Granadan backing)
realms.note: Marrakesh held by the rival Marinid Abd al-Rahman until 1386; Granada strongly influences the court.

realms.name: Hafsid Sultanate
realms.note: Reuniting the Hafsid lands after decades of division.

realms.name: Kingdom of Bohemia (Luxembourg lands)
realms.ruler: Charles IV, Holy Roman Emperor (Wenceslaus IV crowned King of Bohemia and elected King of the Romans)
realms.note: Charles IV dies 29 Nov 1378; Wenceslaus succeeds. Bohemian crown lands include Silesia, Lusatia and Moravia (Jobst, margrave).

realms.name: Margraviate of Brandenburg
realms.ruler: Sigismund of Luxembourg (minor; assigned Brandenburg in his father's 1376–78 settlement)
realms.note: Bought by Charles IV in 1373 and attached to the Bohemian crown; an electoral vote held by the Luxembourgs.

realms.name: Duchy of Brabant
realms.ruler: Joanna and Wenceslaus I of Luxembourg
realms.note: Also holds Limburg.

realms.name: Counties of Holland, Zeeland and Hainaut
realms.ruler: Albert I of Bavaria-Straubing (regent for his insane brother William V)
realms.note: Wittelsbach Bavaria-Straubing line; also holds Straubing in Bavaria.

realms.name: City of Cologne
realms.note: Self-governing since 1288 though not yet formally a free imperial city.

realms.name: Electorate of Saxe-Wittenberg
realms.note: Holds the Saxon electoral vote under the Golden Bull; fighting the Lüneburg succession war.

realms.name: Margraviate of Meissen and Landgraviate of Thuringia (Wettin)
realms.ruler: Frederick III, Balthasar and William I (joint rule)
realms.note: Not yet electors; divided at Chemnitz in 1382.

realms.name: Duchy of Bavaria (Upper and Lower Bavaria-Landshut)
realms.ruler: Stephen III, Frederick and John II (joint rule)
realms.note: Divided in 1392 into Landshut, Ingolstadt and Munich.

realms.name: Duchies of Austria (Habsburg)
realms.ruler: Albert III and Leopold III (joint rule)
realms.note: Austria, Styria, Carinthia, Carniola, Tyrol; split at Neuberg in Sept 1379.

realms.name: Free City of Lübeck
realms.note: Leading city of the Hanse after the Peace of Stralsund (1370).

realms.name: Old Swiss Confederacy (eight cantons)
realms.ruler: No single ruler: diet of Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden, Lucerne, Zürich, Glarus, Zug and Bern

realms.name: State of the Teutonic Order
realms.note: At its height; annual Reisen against pagan Lithuania.

realms.name: Archbishopric of Riga
realms.note: Rival of the Livonian Order for lordship over the city of Riga.

realms.name: Kingdom of Denmark
realms.ruler: Olaf II (child; his mother Margaret governs)
realms.note: Holds Gotland since 1361; Scania regained after Stralsund.

realms.name: Kingdom of Sweden
realms.ruler: Albert of Mecklenburg (power largely with the council magnates, Bo Jonsson Grip)

realms.name: Kingdom of Hungary
realms.note: Also King of Poland; overlord of Ragusa, Vidin, and claimant suzerain of Wallachia, Moldavia and Bosnia.

realms.name: Kingdom of Poland
realms.ruler: Louis I of Hungary (personal union; governors in Poland)
realms.note: Holds Galicia-Ruthenia (Lviv) through Hungarian governors.

realms.name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania
realms.ruler: Jogaila (grand duke since 1377, with his uncle Kęstutis at Trakai)
realms.note: Pagan; rules most of old Rus including Kyiv (under Vladimir Olgerdovich) and Smolensk as a dependency.

realms.name: Principality of Wallachia
realms.ruler: Radu I (succession from Vladislav I c.1377 uncertain)
realms.note: Hungarian suzerainty claimed but not exercised.

realms.name: Moravian Serbia (Lazar)
realms.note: The largest of the Serbian successor lordships after Maritsa (1371).

realms.name: Tsardom of Bulgaria (Tarnovo)
realms.note: Ottoman vassal since c.1376 (his sister Kera Tamara in Murad's household).

realms.name: Byzantine Empire
realms.ruler: Andronikos IV (usurper since Aug 1376; John V and Manuel II imprisoned)
realms.note: Tributary to Murad I; Gallipoli handed back to the Ottomans (1376–77). Holds Thessaloniki, Thracian coast towns and the Morea.

realms.name: Principality of Achaea
realms.ruler: Leased to the Knights Hospitaller (1377–81) by Joanna I
realms.note: Navarrese Company arrives 1378–79.

realms.name: Catalan Duchy of Athens and Neopatras
realms.ruler: Maria of Sicily (title contested by Peter IV of Aragon); vicar-general Luis Fadrique

realms.name: Republic of Venice
realms.note: Holds Crete, Negroponte, Coron and Modon; war with Genoa since spring 1378 (Battle of Antium, 30 May).

realms.name: Republic of Genoa
realms.note: Holds Caffa and the Crimean Gazaria, Pera, Chios (Maona), Famagusta (since 1374).

realms.name: Ottoman Beylik
realms.note: Frontier state in Thrace and northwest Anatolia; overlord of Byzantium and Tarnovo.

realms.name: Beylik of Karaman
realms.ruler: Alaeddin Ali Bey (son-in-law of Murad I)

realms.name: Beylik of Germiyan
realms.note: Its daughter's dowry passes Kütahya to the Ottomans (c.1381).

realms.name: Beylik of Hamid
realms.note: Teke (Antalya) is a separate branch; Hamid sells most of its land to Murad c.1381.

realms.name: Eretnid Sultanate
realms.ruler: Ala al-Din Ali (power with Kadi Burhan al-Din, who takes over in 1381)

realms.name: Kingdom of Cyprus
realms.note: Famagusta held by Genoa since 1374.

realms.name: Knights Hospitaller (Rhodes)
realms.ruler: Grand Master Juan Fernández de Heredia (captive of the Albanians in Epirus, 1378–79)

realms.name: Visconti Milan (Bernabò)
realms.note: The Visconti state is divided: Bernabò rules the east, Gian Galeazzo (from Galeazzo II's death, 4 Aug 1378) the west from Pavia.

realms.name: Visconti Pavia (Gian Galeazzo)
realms.note: Seizes Bernabò and all Milan in May 1385.

realms.name: Verona (della Scala)
realms.ruler: Bartolomeo II and Antonio della Scala

realms.name: Padua (Carrara)
realms.note: Genoa's ally against Venice.

realms.name: Este (Ferrara and Modena)
realms.note: Papal vicars in Ferrara; Modena an imperial fief.

realms.name: Republic of Florence
realms.ruler: Signoria of the Ciompi regime (gonfaloniere Michele di Lando, then Luigi Guicciardini)
realms.note: Just made peace with the Pope after the War of the Eight Saints (Tivoli, July 1378).

realms.name: Papal States
realms.ruler: Pope Urban VI (elected 8 April 1378); Clement VII elected against him at Fondi on 20 Sept
realms.note: Much of the Romagna and Marche held by papal vicars; Castel Sant'Angelo held for Clement until 1379.

realms.name: Comtat Venaissin and Avignon
realms.ruler: Papal rectors (obedience to Clement VII from his arrival in 1379)
realms.note: Clement VII's seat from June 1379.

realms.name: Kingdom of Naples
realms.note: Also Countess of Provence (Marseille) and overlord of Achaea; backs Clement VII.

realms.name: Kingdom of Sicily (Trinacria)
realms.ruler: Maria (child queen) under the Four Vicars: Artale Alagona, Manfredi Chiaramonte, Francesco Ventimiglia, Guglielmo Peralta
realms.note: Palermo governed by Manfredi III Chiaramonte.

realms.name: Judicate of Arborea
realms.note: Holds most of Sardinia against Aragon.

realms.name: Grand Principality of Moscow (Vladimir)
realms.note: Withholding tribute from Mamai; won at the Vozha on 11 Aug 1378.

realms.name: Grand Principality of Ryazan
realms.note: Ravaged by Mamai after the Vozha (Aug 1378).

realms.name: Grand Principality of Nizhny Novgorod-Suzdal
realms.note: Sacked by Arab Shah's Tatars after the Pyana (1377).

realms.name: Golden Horde (Mamai's Horde)
realms.ruler: Beylerbey Mamai, ruling in the name of the puppet khan Muhammad Bolak
realms.note: Holds the steppe west of the Volga and the Crimea; rival khans (Arab Shah, the White Horde) contest Sarai and the Volga.

realms.name: White Horde
realms.ruler: Tokhtamysh (with Timur's backing; the fall of Urus Khan's son Timur-Malik is dated 1378–79)
realms.note: Tokhtamysh takes Sarai c.1380 and unites the Horde after Kulikovo.

realms.name: Mamluk Sultanate
realms.ruler: al-Mansur Ali II (child sultan); power held by the amirs Barquq and Baraka
realms.note: Barquq becomes sultan in 1382.

realms.name: Sharifate of Mecca
realms.ruler: Sharif Ahmad ibn Ajlan (with his father Ajlan)

realms.name: Kingdom of Hormuz
realms.ruler: Malik of Hormuz (name uncertain; Turanshah's line)

realms.name: Qara Qoyunlu
realms.note: Turkmen confederation around Van and Mosul, nominally under the Jalayirids (low confidence).

realms.name: Jalayirid Sultanate
realms.note: Holds Iraq and Azerbaijan (Tabriz) since Shaikh Uvais (d. 1374).

realms.name: Muzaffarid Sultanate
realms.note: Fars, Kerman and Isfahan; briefly took Tabriz in 1375.

realms.name: Kartid Maliks of Herat
realms.note: Timur takes Herat in 1381.

realms.name: Sufid Khwarazm
realms.note: Timur besieges Urgench in 1379.

realms.name: Chagatai Ulus of Timur
realms.note: Transoxiana; his conquests outside it begin in 1379–81.

realms.name: Moghulistan
realms.note: Kashgar governed by the Dughlat amirs.

realms.name: Tughlaq Sultanate of Delhi
realms.note: Still holds Punjab, the Doab, Awadh, Gujarat, Malwa and Multan; breaks up after Firuz dies (1388).

realms.name: Bahmani Sultanate
realms.ruler: Muhammad Shah II (from May 1378, after the murders of Mujahid Shah and Daud Shah)

realms.name: Vijayanagara Empire
realms.note: Has absorbed the Madurai Sultanate (by c.1378).

realms.name: Kingdom of Gampola
realms.ruler: Bhuvanaikabahu V (power with the minister Alagakkonara at Kotte)

realms.name: Nepal (Malla)
realms.ruler: Jayarjuna Malla (Jayasthiti Malla the power behind him; takes the throne 1382)

realms.name: Northern Yuan
realms.ruler: Uskhal Khan Tögüs Temür (from May 1378, after Biligtü Khan Ayushiridara)
realms.note: Karakorum is burned by Ming in 1380.

realms.name: Yuan Prince of Liang (Yunnan)
realms.note: Ming conquers Yunnan in 1381–82; Dali still under the Duan family.

realms.name: Naghachu's Manchuria
realms.note: Surrenders to Ming in 1387.

realms.name: Goryeo
realms.ruler: King U (Yi Seong-gye and Choe Yeong the leading generals)
realms.note: Wokou raids at their height.

realms.name: Southern Court of Japan
realms.note: Prince Kaneyoshi's Kyushu base lost to Imagawa Ryōshun from 1372.

realms.name: Chūzan
realms.note: Ming tributary since 1372.

realms.name: Đại Việt (Trần)
realms.ruler: Trần Phế Đế (senior emperor Trần Nghệ Tông; Hồ Quý Ly rising)
realms.note: Thăng Long sacked by Champa in 1371 and again 1377–78.

realms.name: Champa
realms.note: At war with Đại Việt; killed King Trần Duệ Tông in 1377.

realms.name: Khmer Kingdom
realms.ruler: King at Angkor (name uncertain in the chronicles)

realms.name: Sukhothai
realms.note: Submitted to Ayutthaya in 1378.

realms.name: Majapahit
realms.note: At its height; claims tribute across the archipelago (Nagarakretagama, 1365).

realms.name: Singapura (Temasek)
realms.note: Listed as a Majapahit tributary (1365); also pressed by Ayutthaya.

realms.name: Mali Empire
realms.ruler: Mansa Musa II (power with the vizier Mari Djata)
realms.note: Holds Timbuktu, Walata and Gao; capital site disputed.

realms.name: Kanem (Sayfawa)
realms.ruler: Sayfawa mai (several killed by the Bulala c.1376–82)
realms.note: Losing Kanem to the Bulala; withdraws to Bornu c.1380s.

realms.name: Sultanate of Ifat
realms.note: At war with Ethiopia.

realms.name: Kilwa Sultanate
realms.ruler: Sultan of the Mahdali line (name uncertain)

realms.name: Great Zimbabwe
realms.note: Near its height.

realms.name: Purépecha (Tarascan) lordships
realms.ruler: Tangáxuan I (with Hiripan at Ihuatzio and Hiquíngare at Pátzcuaro; low confidence)

realms.name: Kingdom of Cusco
realms.ruler: Sapa Inca of the Hurin/Hanan line (Inca Roca? low confidence)

nantes.note: Duke John IV in exile; French royal garrisons held much of Brittany 1373–79, and Charles V had the duchy confiscated in Dec 1378. Could be read as French.

marseille.note: County of Provence held by Joanna I of Naples in personal union.

dublin.note: Lordship of Ireland under the English Crown's justiciar.

amsterdam.note: County of Holland under Albert of Bavaria-Straubing.

ceuta.note: Marinid; Granada occupies it briefly in 1384–87.

algiers.note: Contested between the Zayyanids, the Hafsids and the local Tha'aliba Arabs.

milan.note: Bernabò's seat; the city itself was shared between the two Visconti branches, Gian Galeazzo ruling from Pavia.

rome.note: Castel Sant'Angelo held by a Clementist garrison until April 1379.

palermo.note: Governed by the vicar Manfredi III Chiaramonte in the name of Queen Maria.

cologne.note: The city governs itself against its archbishop; formal free-city status only in 1475.

bern.note: Canton of Bern, member of the eight-canton Confederacy since 1353.

copenhagen.note: Town held as a fief by the Bishop of Roskilde until 1417.

visby.note: Danish since 1361 but largely autonomous; Mecklenburg Sweden claims Gotland.

riga.note: City lordship contested between the Archbishop and the Livonian Order (Order dominant 1330–66); the city itself a self-governing Hanse town.

kyiv.note: Appanage of Vladimir Olgerdovich under the Grand Duke.

kazan.note: Volga Bulgar emirs (forced to pay tribute to Moscow in 1376) under the fragmented Horde.

astrakhan.note: Hajji Tarkhan changed hands among rival Horde khans and local lords in the 1370s.

sarai.note: Contested during the Great Troubles: Arab Shah held the Volga c.1377–80, Mamai the west; Tokhtamysh takes it c.1380.

sofia.note: Falls to the Ottomans in 1382 or 1385.

athens.note: Nerio Acciaioli takes the Acropolis in 1388.

thessaloniki.note: Byzantine; which faction of the civil war it obeyed in 1376–79 is unclear.

constantinople.note: Andronikos IV's capital until John V retakes it in July 1379.

kabul.note: Within the Chagatai ulus; how firmly Timur controlled Kabul by 1378 is unclear.

jaunpur.note: Founded by Firuz Shah c.1359; independent only from 1394.

ahmedabad.note: Tughlaq province of Gujarat; Ahmedabad not yet founded (Asaval).

colombo.note: Alagakkonara's Kotte stronghold nearby; Jaffna's officials also collected dues on the west coast.

shenyang.note: Ming Liaodong command at Liaoyang since 1371; the Shenyang area was exposed to Naghachu's raids and its guard was set up only in 1386.

seoul.note: Hanyang, a secondary capital of Goryeo.

hakata.note: Under the Kyushu tandai Imagawa Ryōshun since 1372.

shuri.note: Chūzan's capital was still Urasoe; Shuri becomes the seat c.1406.

malacca.note: Not yet founded (c.1400); coast in the sphere of Majapahit and Ayutthaya.

manila.note: Manila Bay polities (Tondo, Maynila) are poorly attested before c.1500.

gao.note: Under Mali; the Sunni rulers of Songhai may already have been loosening Malian control.

niani.note: The site of Mali's capital is disputed.

kanem.note: Sayfawa mais were being killed in succession by the Bulala; Njimi is abandoned in the 1380s.

mbanza_kongo.note: Kongo kingdom founded c.1390 (Lukeni lua Nimi); before that Mpemba Kasi and Mbata chiefdoms.

tzintzuntzan.note: Tarascan lordships divided among Tariácuri's heirs; chronology uncertain.

havana.note: Taíno and Guanahatabey chiefdoms, no state.

quito.note: Local lords; whether they formed a state is disputed.

bogota.note: The Bacatá zipazgo is traditionally dated from c.1450; earlier Muisca chiefdoms.

quebec.note: St Lawrence Iroquoian villages, no state.

Battle of Reutlingen (Swabian City League beats Württemberg)
Death of Algirdas; Jogaila grand duke of Lithuania

open_questions: Brittany: whether Nantes counts as ducal (John IV in exile) or French (royal occupation 1373–79, confiscation Dec 1378).
Golden Horde: who held Sarai, Hajji Tarkhan (Astrakhan) and Bulgar/Kazan in Sept 1378 (Mamai, Arab Shah, Urus Khan's heirs or local lords) is unclear; all given to Mamai's Horde at low confidence.
White Horde: whether Tokhtamysh had already displaced Timur-Malik by Sept 1378 (sources date it 1377–79).
Wallachia: Vladislav I's death and Radu I's accession are dated c.1374–77; Hungarian suzerainty nominal.
Serbia: whether Lazar was an Ottoman tributary before Kosovo is disputed; left with no overlord.
Byzantium: Andronikos IV holds Constantinople; the obedience of Thessaloniki during the civil war is unclear.
Riga: contested lordship between Archbishop and Livonian Order; low confidence.
Algiers: Zayyanid, Hafsid or local Tha'aliba control in 1378 uncertain.
Kanem: how much of Kanem the Sayfawa still held against the Bulala in 1378.
Kabul and Shenyang: degree of Timur's and Ming's control uncertain.
Visconti Milan treated as two realms (Bernabò and Gian Galeazzo); Milan city itself was shared.
Castile and Aragon had not yet declared an obedience; Castile went to Avignon in 1381, Aragon in 1387.
Many rulers outside Europe and the Islamic world (Khmer, Kilwa, Benin, Cusco, Chimor, Tarascans, Ryukyu kings) are uncertain or unknown.

Realm ids harmonised across all checkpoints (see ids.json): the Golden Horde uses great_horde from 1378 on, the League of Mayapan uses maya, Azcapotzalco uses tepanecs, Chūzan uses ryukyu, Gampola uses kotte, the Catalan duchy uses athens and the Comtat Venaissin uses avignon_papacy, so each state keeps one id.
